speaker: interviewer
text: Hi Kenji, thanks for joining. Are the kids around?

speaker: interviewee
text: They're at nursery, so we have a quiet hour, which is a miracle.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha, great. So there are no wrong answers, this is about your orders.

speaker: interviewee
text: Sure.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me a bit about your household and who does the food shopping.

speaker: interviewee
text: Me, my wife Lena and our twins, they're four. We both work full time, I'm an architect, she's in insurance. We split the shopping, which in practice means whoever is least tired orders on the app on Sunday night.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. Walk me through your last Shmuber Eats order, from opening the app to putting things away.

speaker: interviewee
text: Sunday night, Lena started the basket, I added the rest. Milk, a lot of milk, fruit, yogurts, pasta, chicken, the bread the kids like. We hit order, it came Monday evening. I put it away while she did bath time.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. How often do you order groceries online?

speaker: interviewee
text: Every week now, since the summer. Before that we'd go together on Saturday, with the twins in the trolley, which was like a sport.

speaker: interviewer
text: And what made you start every week?

speaker: interviewee
text: Honestly, Saturdays. We wanted them back. A whole morning in the supermarket with four-year-olds, you lose the day.

speaker: interviewer
text: Got it. How do you keep track of what you need between orders?

speaker: interviewee
text: There's the list in your app, we both add to it. Lena adds during the week, I add on Sunday. Sometimes we both add milk and get eight litres.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. Does anyone else add?

speaker: interviewee
text: My mother, when she babysits, she tells Lena and Lena adds it. So indirectly.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Tell me about the last time an item in your order was substituted.

speaker: interviewee
text: It happens most weeks, something small. A different yogurt, a different brand of pasta. Usually fine. The twins notice the yogurt, they're very strict.

speaker: interviewer
text: Wouldn't it be great if we texted you before swapping anything, so you could say yes or no?

speaker: interviewee
text: Yeah, I mean, maybe. If I'm at the office, sure, I'd answer. If it's bath time, nobody is looking at a phone.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. How did you pick the delivery window last time?

speaker: interviewee
text: Six to eight on Monday, always the same. One of us is home by six.

speaker: interviewer
text: And do you ever miss it?

speaker: interviewee
text: Once. Lena was stuck on a train. The driver left it with the neighbour, which was lucky.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. What would you think of a monthly delivery pass, and what would you pay for it?

speaker: interviewee
text: We'd probably do it. We order every week, so the delivery fees add up. Maybe seven or eight a month.

speaker: interviewee
text: Hmm. Probably still, yeah. It's less than four delivery fees, right? I'd have to check.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great, great. Would you recommend Shmuber Eats to a friend?

speaker: interviewee
text: Already did. Two families from nursery use it now.

speaker: interviewer
text: Amazing. What do you like most?

speaker: interviewee
text: Getting Saturday back. That's it, that's the whole review.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha. And what do you like least?

speaker: interviewee
text: The app forgets the regular order. I wish I could just say same as last week and change two things.

speaker: interviewer
text: Noted, repeat order. Great. Have you ever contacted support?

speaker: interviewee
text: No, never. I nearly did once, for taco night. I'd asked for plain flour tortillas, and the picker swapped them for chili-lime ones, the spicy red kind, for taco night with two four-year-olds.

speaker: interviewer
text: Chili-lime for the twins? How did that go?

speaker: interviewee
text: Tears. Both of them. I had to make them toast while Lena and I ate the spicy tacos.

speaker: interviewer
text: What would you have wanted the picker to do instead?

speaker: interviewee
text: Just leave it out, honestly. Or pick plain ones from another brand. The point was plain, not tortilla.

speaker: interviewer
text: Great. Last question, is there anything about your orders I didn't ask about?

speaker: interviewee
text: Maybe the bags. We have so many paper bags we built a castle out of them.

speaker: interviewer
text: Haha, noted. Thank you so much, Kenji.

speaker: interviewee
text: No problem, bye.
